subject: physics

sections.title: Introduction to Atomic Physics
learning_objectives: Describe the basic structure of the atom, the substructure of all matter.

sections.title: The Pauli Exclusion Principle
learning_objectives: Define the composition of an atom along with its electrons, neutrons, and protons.
Explain the Pauli exclusion principle and its application to the atom.
Specify the shell and subshell symbols and their positions.
Define the position of electrons in different shells of an atom.
State the position of each element in the periodic table according to shell filling.

sections.title: Discovery of the Atom
learning_objectives: Describe the basic structure of the atom, the substructure of all matter.

sections.title: Discovery of the Parts of the Atom: Electrons and Nuclei
learning_objectives: Describe how electrons were discovered.
Explain the Millikan oil drop experiment.
Describe Rutherford’s gold foil experiment.
Describe Rutherford’s planetary model of the atom.

sections.title: Bohr’s Theory of the Hydrogen Atom
learning_objectives: Describe the mysteries of atomic spectra.
Explain Bohr’s theory of the hydrogen atom.
Explain Bohr’s planetary model of the atom.
Illustrate energy state using the energy-level diagram.
Describe the triumphs and limits of Bohr’s theory.

sections.title: X Rays: Atomic Origins and Applications
learning_objectives: Define x-ray tube and its spectrum.
Show the x-ray characteristic energy.
Specify the use of x rays in medical observations.
Explain the use of x rays in CT scanners in diagnostics.

sections.title: Applications of Atomic Excitations and De-Excitations
learning_objectives: Define and discuss fluorescence.
Define metastable.
Describe how laser emission is produced.
Explain population inversion.
Define and discuss holography.

sections.title: The Wave Nature of Matter Causes Quantization
learning_objectives: Explain Bohr’s model of atom.
Define and describe quantization of angular momentum.
Calculate the angular momentum for an orbit of atom.
Define and describe the wave-like properties of matter.

sections.title: Patterns in Spectra Reveal More Quantization
learning_objectives: State and discuss the Zeeman effect.
Define orbital magnetic field.
Define orbital angular momentum.
Define space quantization.

sections.title: Quantum Numbers and Rules
learning_objectives: Define quantum number.
Calculate angle of angular momentum vector with an axis.
Define spin quantum number.

sections.title: Introduction to Quantum Physics
learning_objectives: Explain Max Planck’s contribution to the development of quantum mechanics.

sections.title: Quantization of Energy
learning_objectives: Explain Max Planck’s contribution to the development of quantum mechanics.
Explain why atomic spectra indicate quantization.

sections.title: The Photoelectric Effect
learning_objectives: Describe a typical photoelectric-effect experiment.

Determine the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons ejected by photons of one energy or wavelength, when given the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons for a different photon energy or wavelength.

sections.title: Photon Energies and the Electromagnetic Spectrum
learning_objectives: Explain the relationship between the energy of a photon in joules or electron volts and its wavelength or frequency.
Calculate the number of photons per second emitted by a monochromatic source of specific wavelength and power.

sections.title: Photon Momentum
learning_objectives: Relate the linear momentum of a photon to its energy or wavelength, and apply linear momentum conservation to simple processes involving the emission, absorption, or reflection of photons.
Account qualitatively for the increase of photon wavelength that is observed, and explain the significance of the Compton wavelength.

sections.title: The Particle-Wave Duality
learning_objectives: Explain what the term particle-wave duality means, and why it is applied to EM radiation.

sections.title: The Wave Nature of Matter
learning_objectives: Describe the Davisson-Germer experiment, and explain how it provides evidence for the wave nature of electrons.

sections.title: Probability: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle
learning_objectives: Use both versions of Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle in calculations.
Explain the implications of Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle for measurements.

sections.title: The Particle-Wave Duality Reviewed
learning_objectives: Explain the concept of particle-wave duality, and its scope.

sections.title: Introduction to Radioactivity and Nuclear Physics
learning_objectives: Explain nuclear radiation.

sections.title: Nuclear Radioactivity
learning_objectives: Explain nuclear radiation.
Explain the types of radiation—alpha emission, beta emission, and gamma emission.
Explain the ionization of radiation in an atom.
Define the range of radiation.

sections.title: Radiation Detection and Detectors
learning_objectives: Explain the working principle of a Geiger tube.
Define and discuss radiation detectors.

sections.title: Substructure of the Nucleus
learning_objectives: Define and discuss the nucleus in an atom.
Define atomic number.
Define and discuss isotopes.
Calculate the density of the nucleus.
Explain nuclear force.

sections.title: Nuclear Decay and Conservation Laws
learning_objectives: Define and discuss nuclear decay.
State the conservation laws.
Explain parent and daughter nucleus.
Calculate the energy emitted during nuclear decay.

sections.title: Half-Life and Activity
learning_objectives: Define half-life.
Define dating.
Calculate age of old objects by radioactive dating.

sections.title: Binding Energy
learning_objectives: Define and discuss binding energy.
Calculate the binding energy per nucleon of a particle.

sections.title: Tunneling
learning_objectives: Define and discuss tunneling.
Define potential barrier.
Explain quantum tunneling.
